keyQuestions: What security measures must be in place?
What compliance requirements are relevant?
files.content:
# Security and Compliance Requirements for Todo List Application

## Access Control Policies

Access controls define business-driven boundaries for system usage, protecting user data and upholding privacy obligations.

### User Authentication and Authorization
- WHEN a user attempts to access any service feature, THE application SHALL require authentication using valid, unique user credentials (e.g., email and password).
- WHEN a user authenticates, THE system SHALL generate a secure session using a robust mechanism, such as JWT, valid for a limited and configurable period.
- WHEN a user is not authenticated and requests a protected resource, THE system SHALL deny the request and prompt for authentication.
- WHEN a user accesses, edits, or deletes a todo item, THE system SHALL verify the user's identity and grant permission ONLY if the todo belongs to that user OR if the user has administrative privileges.
- WHEN a user attempts to modify another user's todos or account, THE system SHALL reject the request unless the user is an admin.
- WHEN a user logs out, THE system SHALL immediately revoke any active tokens for that user and end the session.
- WHEN a session expires or presents an invalid token, THE system SHALL deny access and require re-authentication.
- User roles SHALL be enforced for all business actions:
  - Regular users SHALL operate solely on their own data (todos, account info, etc.).
  - Admin users SHALL have access to all todo and user data for management, audit, and monitoring purposes.

#### Permission Matrix
| Feature / Action                                | User | Admin |
|------------------------------------------------|------|-------|
| View own todos                                 | ✅   | ✅    |
| Create/modify/delete own todos                 | ✅   | ✅    |
| View/modify/delete others' todos               | ❌   | ✅    |
| Manage user accounts                           | ❌   | ✅    |
| Access system health reports                   | ❌   | ✅    |
| Export own data                                | ✅   | ✅    |
| Export all user data                           | ❌   | ✅    |
| Manage/compliance audit logs                   | ❌   | ✅    |

#### Role Violation Handling
- WHEN a user attempts an unauthorized action (outside their role), THE system SHALL deny the request, log the incident (with user, action, timestamp), and display a clear error message.
- WHEN repeated unauthorized actions are detected from the same user, THE system SHALL alert an administrator for possible review.

### Session and Token Management
- WHEN a session token is issued, THE system SHALL include user ID, roles, and explicit permission claims in the token payload, with secure signature and encryption.
- WHEN a session is idle for over 30 minutes (configurable), THE system SHALL expire the session and require user re-authentication.
- WHEN logout is triggered by the user or admin, THE system SHALL provide logout from all sessions/devices.
- THE system SHALL allow revocation of tokens at any time by either the user (for own account) or admins (for any user).

## Data Protection and Security Standards

### Sensitive Data Handling
- WHEN saving or processing any personal data—including names, emails, credentials, todo content—THE system SHALL treat all such data as sensitive and SHALL:
  - Store passwords ONLY as one-way, salted hashes using modern algorithms (bcrypt, Argon2, or equivalent)
  - Transmit all sensitive data exclusively over encrypted TLS connections
  - NEVER log, display, or expose raw credentials/tokens outside secured and ephemeral memory areas
  - Enforce least-privilege access throughout UI/API exposure—users see only their own todo data; admins see all

### Data Encryption
- WHEN storing sensitive data at rest (including tokens, password hashes), THE system SHALL use strong encryption algorithms and maintain secure key management with rotation and compromise response procedures.
- WHEN regulatory or high-security requirements apply, THE system SHALL allow for configurable encryption keys and policies.

### Data Minimization and Retention
- WHEN user data is no longer needed, THE system SHALL enable permanent deletion upon user request, subject to legal retention obligations.
- WHEN a user requests account or todo deletion, THE system SHALL irreversibly remove associated data barring legal requirements for further retention.
- WHEN a user requests data export, THE system SHALL process and deliver a copy, responding within required business timeframes (e.g., 30 days by default, configurable).
- THE system SHALL keep audit logs of all admin actions affecting more than one user, with a one-year minimum retention for compliance as a business standard.

### Monitoring, Logging, and Intrusion Detection
- WHEN authentication attempts, record updates, or access violations occur, THE system SHALL log these events, including timestamp, resource(s), user, and result.
- WHEN logs reference user activity, THE system SHALL ensure that no sensitive data (e.g., passwords, raw tokens, personal messages) is stored within them.
- WHEN suspicious activity patterns (e.g., multiple failed logins, token abuse) are detected, THE system SHALL notify an admin for review.
- WHEN a potential intrusion or security breach is detected, THE system SHALL escalate to compliance and management immediately and initiate incident response.

### Security Best Practices
- THE application SHALL adhere to industry best practices—regular dependency updates, strong HTTP security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options), and limited lifespan for access tokens.
- WHEN a security update is released, THE development and operations teams SHALL apply patches within a business-determined, risk-based timeframe (e.g., within 7 days for critical vulnerabilities).

## Compliance Obligations

### GDPR and Global Privacy Alignment
- WHEN collecting, processing, or storing user PII, THE system SHALL uphold users' data subject rights: access, rectification, erasure, portability, objection, restriction, and withdrawal of consent.
- WHEN a user first interacts with the Todo List application, THE system SHALL present a clear privacy notice explaining data use and protection.
- WHEN obtaining user consent for data processing, THE system SHALL implement a mechanism for users to review and withdraw consent at any time.
- WHEN handling data breaches affecting user rights/freedoms, THE system SHALL enable business processes for notifying users and regulatory authorities promptly and within regulatory deadlines.

### Other Privacy and Compliance Standards
- THE system SHALL embed privacy by design, incorporating data protection into all development and operational processes as a business priority.
- WHEN operating across multiple regions or jurisdictions, THE application SHALL enable restricting data transfers to only compliant regions/countries.
- WHEN legally required, THE system SHALL apply specialized policies (e.g., CCPA, PIPA) based on user locality.
- Compliance and audit logs SHALL be available to authorized business or legal officers for regulatory inquiries, audit trails, or internal reviews.

## Mermaid Diagram: Security Workflow Overview
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "User Session & Access Flow"
    A["User Authentication"] --> B["Role Validation"]
    B -->|"User"| C["Access Own Data Only"]
    B -->|"Admin"| D["Access All Users' Data"]
    C --> E["Session Management"]
    D --> E
    E --> F{"Request Scope Check"}
    F -->|"Within Role"| G["Permission Granted"]
    F -->|"Violation"| H["Log Violation & Deny"]
  end
  subgraph "Data Protection"
    I["PII Encryption at Rest/Transit"]
    J["Audit Logging"]
    K["Token Issuance"]
  end
  G --> I
  G --> K
  H --> J
```

## Summary for Implementation
All requirements listed are mandatory for the Todo List application's backend development, forming the legal and business-driven foundation for design and operational workflows. Requirements use unambiguous business language and EARS-compliant statements to remove ambiguity for backend engineers and promote testable, enterprise-grade security and privacy features.

files.reason: To define the conceptual flow and lifecycle of information within the service, describing data creation, update, retrieval, and removal in business terms.
keyQuestions: How does data move through the system in user terms?
What is the expected lifecycle of a todo item?
files.content:
# Todo List Application Requirements – Data Flow & Lifecycle

## Data Creation Process

A todo item begins its lifecycle when a user or admin creates it. The system distinguishes between standard users and admins in terms of permissions, logging, and error recovery.

**User Actor – user**
- WHEN a user, authenticated by the system, submits a request to create a new todo, THE system SHALL validate that todo content is not empty and does not exceed maximum character length (configurable, e.g., 255 characters).
- WHEN validation passes, THE system SHALL create a new todo entry linked to the user's account, store a creation timestamp, and mark the todo as "incomplete" by default.
- IF a user submits a todo with empty content or content exceeding maximum length, THEN THE system SHALL reject the request with a user-friendly error message.
- IF a non-authenticated user attempts creation, THEN THE system SHALL deny the request and respond with an authentication prompt.

**User Actor – admin**
- WHEN an admin creates a todo (e.g., for testing, demonstration, or user support), THE system SHALL record the admin as the actor in the audit log and link the correct user if creating on behalf of another account.

**Business Rules**
- THE system SHALL NOT permit the creation of duplicate (identical content and due date) incompleted todos by the same user.

```mermaid
graph LR
  A["User Submits New Todo"] --> B{"Authenticated?"}
  B -->|"No"| C["Reject: Prompt Login"]
  B -->|"Yes"| D["Validate Content"]
  D --> E{"Content Valid?"}
  E -->|"No"| F["Reject: Validation Error"]
  E -->|"Yes"| G["Create Todo (Status: Incomplete)"]
  G --> H["Confirmation/Success"]
```

## Data Update/Modification Flow

Users and admins may update todo records—modifying content, metadata, or status. Permissions and business validation rules safeguard data integrity at all times.

**User Actor – user**
- WHEN a user edits or updates their own todo, THE system SHALL validate that modified content is not empty and meets all length restrictions before saving changes.
- WHEN a user marks a todo as complete/incomplete, THE system SHALL record the updated status and timestamp the operation.
- IF a user tries to modify or complete a todo they do not own, THEN THE system SHALL deny the request, returning a permissions error.
- IF a user tries to update a deleted or non-existent todo, THEN THE system SHALL refuse the update and present a not found error.
- WHEN a user modifies a todo’s due date, THE system SHALL ensure the new date is not in the past relative to the current date/time.

**User Actor – admin**
- WHEN an admin updates any todo, THE system SHALL log the operation, including the actor and modification details, for auditing.
- WHEN an admin marks a user’s todo as complete/incomplete, THE system SHALL document the change and include contextual audit data.
- WHERE admins respond to disputes or abuse reports, THE system SHALL allow admin correction/updating of user todo, with all such actions fully traceable.

**Business Rules**
- THE system SHALL prevent setting content to empty during any modification.
- THE system SHALL only allow updates to valid, non-deleted todos.

```mermaid
graph LR
  A["User Requests Todo Update"] --> B{"User is Owner or Admin?"}
  B -->|"No"| C["Reject: Permission Denied"]
  B -->|"Yes"| D["Validate Update (e.g., Non-emptiness, Date)"]
  D --> E{"Valid?"}
  E -->|"No"| F["Reject: Validation/Error"]
  E -->|"Yes"| G["Apply Update & Record Timestamp"]
  G --> H["Success/Confirmation"]
```

## Data Retrieval and Filtering

The retrieval process enables users and admins to access todo information based on access level, search criteria, and filtering.

**User Actor – user**
- WHEN a user requests their todo list, THE system SHALL return only todos owned by that user.
- WHEN a user applies filters (completion status, keyword search, date range), THE system SHALL restrict queries to that user's records.
- IF a user accesses data not owned by them, THEN THE system SHALL block access and return a privacy error message.
- WHEN paginating, THE system SHALL sort results by creation date, latest first.

**User Actor – admin**
- WHEN an admin requests todos, THE system SHALL allow full access, enabling filtering by user, status, or date.
- WHEN searching, THE system SHALL permit admin-level search across all user todo records. Auditing and activity review are supported by relevant filters.

**Business Rules**
- THE system SHALL restrict data returns according to the requestor's permissions.
- THE system SHALL enable searching, filtering, and pagination per business requirements.

```mermaid
graph LR
  A["User/Admin Requests Todo List"] --> B{"User or Admin?"}
  B -->|"User"| C["List Own Todos Only"]
  B -->|"Admin"| D["List Todos (All Users)"]
  C --> E{"Filter/Keyword?"}
  D --> F{"Filter/Keyword?"}
  E -->|"Yes"| G["Apply User-Level Filters/Search"]
  F -->|"Yes"| H["Apply System-Wide Filters/Search"]
  E -->|"No"| I["Return All Own Todos"]
  F -->|"No"| J["Return All Todos"]
```

## Data Deletion and Retention

This process governs removal of todos and the lifespan of task data. Retention, recovery, and compliance are outlined here.

**User Actor – user**
- WHEN a user deletes their own todo, THE system SHALL mark it as deleted, record a deletion timestamp, and allow recovery for a retention window of 7 days (soft delete).
- IF a user tries deleting a todo they do not own, THEN THE system SHALL reject the action and return a permission error.
- WHEN a retention window expires, THE system SHALL hard-delete the todo, permanently removing it and its associated data.
- IF a user attempts to recover a hard-deleted todo, THEN THE system SHALL not find it and return an unrecoverable status.

**User Actor – admin**
- WHEN an admin deletes todos, THE system SHALL log the actor, reason (if provided), and operation in the system audit log.
- WHERE a legal/compliance hold exists, THE system SHALL prevent hard deletion until the hold expires.
- WHEN admins view deleted tasks, THE system SHALL provide filter/search options for all deleted and in-retention-period items.

**Business Rules**
- THE system SHALL soft delete tasks by default; hard delete occurs only after retention expiration.
- THE system SHALL maintain an audit log on every deletion and recovery action (actor, timestamp, reason).
- THE system SHALL display user-friendly retention and recovery info at time of deletion.

```mermaid
graph LR
  A["User/Admin Requests Todo Deletion"] --> B{"User is Owner or Admin?"}
  B -->|"No"| C["Reject: Permission Denied"]
  B -->|"Yes"| D["Soft Delete: Mark as Deleted, Start Retention"]
  D --> E{"Undo/Recover within 7 Days?"}
  E -->|"Yes"| F["Restore Todo"]
  E -->|"No"| G["Hard Delete after 7 Days"]
  G --> H["Permanently Remove Data"]
```

## Full Todo Lifecycle Overview

A todo item typically experiences:
1. Creation – With validation and actor association.
2. Update/modification – With owner checks and audit logging.
3. Retrieval – Permissioned, filtered access.
4. Soft delete – Hides from standard views, retains recoverability for 7 days.
5. Hard delete – Irreversible removal post-retention, with audit trail.

```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Create Todo"] --> B["Active (Incomplete/Complete)"]
  B --> C["Modify/Update"]
  C --> B
  B --> D["Soft Delete"]
  D --> E{"Recovered within 7 Days?"}
  E -->|"Yes"| B
  E -->|"No"| F["Hard Delete"]
```

## Appendix: Terminology
- **Soft delete:** Temporarily hiding a todo for user recovery.
- **Hard delete:** Permanent erasure of a todo and its data after retention.
- **Retention period:** The time window in which a deleted todo may be recovered (7 days by default).
- **Audit log:** Security/compliance record of all todo creation, modification, and deletion activities, including timestamps and responsible actors.

files.reason: To explain important domain-specific terminology and definitions for todo application stakeholders, fostering shared understanding and reducing ambiguity.
files.content:
# Glossary of Terms for Todo List Application

## Introduction

Effective collaboration between all stakeholders of the Todo List Application—developers, testers, business managers, and end users—relies on a shared understanding of terminology. Ambiguous or conflicting definitions can result in communication breakdowns, missed requirements, and software defects. The purpose of this glossary is to offer definitive explanations for key terms and concepts referenced throughout all project documentation, ensuring that business requirements, design, development, and testing are consistently aligned. The audience for this glossary includes every participant involved with the application, irrespective of technical background. Each term included here is rigorously defined to be clear, unambiguous, and actionable. When a term from this glossary appears in requirement or process documents, it always refers to the explanation provided here.

## Key Terms and Definitions

| Term                  | Definition                                                                                                                      |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Todo List             | A personal or shared collection of actionable tasks that a user manages and tracks for individual or collaborative purposes.    |
| Task / Todo Item      | A single actionable unit within a Todo List, representing a specific activity, responsibility, or reminder.                     |
| User                  | An individual registered within the Todo application who can create, manage, edit, and track their own Todo Items.              |
| Admin                 | A privileged user responsible for system administration, monitoring, and the management of all application users and data.      |
| Task Creation         | The process by which a user or admin adds a new Todo Item to a Todo List.                                                      |
| Task Editing          | The ability to modify the content or properties of an existing Todo Item.                                                      |
| Task Deletion         | The act of permanently removing a Todo Item from the Todo List.                                                                |
| Task Completion       | The process of marking a Todo Item as finished or done, reflecting that no further action on this task is required.            |
| Mark as Complete      | The action to update the status of a Todo Item to indicate that it has been accomplished.                                      |
| Overdue Task          | A Todo Item that has a due date which has passed without being marked as completed by the user.                                |
| Active Task           | A Todo Item that is yet to be completed and is not overdue.                                                                   |
| Task Status           | A categorical state of a Todo Item, typically including: active, completed, and optionally overdue.                            |
| Due Date              | The specific date and/or time by which a Todo Item should be completed.                                                        |
| Priority Level        | A designation (e.g., Low, Medium, High) that indicates the relative importance or urgency of a Todo Item.                        |
| Task Filter           | A user-applied control that limits the visible Todo Items to a certain criteria, such as status, due date, or priority.        |
| Search Function       | The ability to find specific Todo Items matching user-defined text or parameters.                                               |
| List View             | The display interface showing the current set of Todo Items, possibly sorted, grouped, or filtered per user settings.           |
| User Authentication   | The process through which users verify their identity (e.g., by logging in) to access their personal Todo List and account.     |
| User Profile          | The collection of information and settings associated with a registered user (e.g., name, email, preferences).                  |
| Account Management    | The set of user actions associated with changing personal or security information, or controlling access to the application.    |
| Permission            | A user’s right to perform a certain action within the application, defined based on the user’s actor type (User or Admin).      |
| Session               | The period during which a user's authentication is valid, allowing ongoing access to their Todo List and actions.                |
| Task Ownership        | The association that each Todo Item is exclusively managed and visible to its creator, unless explicitly shared or changed.     |
| Data Retention Policy | Business rule outlining how long user and Todo Item data is stored before being deleted or archived.                            |
| Error Handling        | The system’s process for detecting, reporting, and guiding user recovery from errors or exceptional events.                     |
| Recovery Flow         | The user journey from encountering an error or failure to successful task completion or resolution.                             |
| Non-Functional Requirement | A system quality or constraint not directly tied to user feature requests, such as performance, scalability, or security.      |
| Authentication Token  | A secure, unique value (such as JWT) issued upon successful login, enabling a user to maintain an authorized session.           |
| Permission Matrix     | A tabular mapping of allowed or restricted actions for each user actor in the system.                                          |
| Business Rule         | A policy or constraint defining system logic, such as what constitutes task completion, deletion, or priority.                 |
| Workflow              | The ordered set of actions through which users accomplish tasks within the Todo application.                                    |
| Validation Constraint | A check or rule ensuring input data to the system meets expected format or business logic, preventing improper data entry.      |
| Filtering             | The ability for a user to view only specific Todo Items according to selected criteria.                                        |
| CRUD                  | Acronym for Create, Read, Update, Delete—the four fundamental actions to manage Todo Items.                                   |
| Status Update         | Action of changing the state of a Todo Item, such as marking it as completed or reverting it to active.                        |
| Data Lifecycle        | The stages through which data passes: creation, active use, update, archival, and deletion.                                    |

## Usage Guidelines

- Users, business analysts, and developers SHALL always reference this glossary when encountering domain terms in requirements, specifications, or user stories to ensure consistent interpretation.
- WHEN developing, reviewing, or updating requirements documents, THE team SHALL verify that any domain-specific term is defined here, and if not, SHALL propose a definition for stakeholder approval before further progress.
- WHEN a project document refers to a term from this glossary, THE intended meaning SHALL be that given here, and ambiguity SHALL be resolved using these definitions.
- Maintain this glossary as a living document; WHEN new business concepts arise during the system's lifecycle, definitions SHALL be refined, added, or clarified through stakeholder review.

## Scope and Boundaries

- This glossary is strictly limited to business and user-facing terms relevant to the Todo List Application’s features and operation.
- It DOES NOT provide technical specification, implementation details, or programming concepts not directly referenced in end-user or business requirements.
- The glossary SHALL NOT serve as a database schema or API documentation resource.

## Cross-References

- All other requirement documents, user scenarios, and workflow diagrams for the Todo List Application SHALL reference the terms in this glossary.
- WHEN new requirement documents are added, THE author SHALL ensure all non-obvious terms are cross-referenced here or proposed as additions.

## Change Process

- Propose additions, clarifications, or corrections to this glossary via stakeholder meetings, requirement review sessions, or change requests.
- Review and update the glossary in regular project retrospectives and as part of the release planning process to ensure accurate, up-to-date definitions are available for all stakeholders.

models.name: todo_list_system_settings
models.description:
System-wide application configuration and global settings table.

Provides a centralized location for storing key/value pairs, flags, and operational parameters used by the todo list application at runtime. Each row represents a distinct configuration setting. This allows for reliable, auditable modification and retrieval of system-level options, feature toggles, and environment variables.

Typical usage includes storing site-wide feature switches, maintenance flags, version numbers, and other application settings that need to be referenced by business logic or admin operations. Settings can be updated as the product evolves or undergoes upgrades, with timestamps preserving the history of changes.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Uniquely identifies each configuration record.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Unique setting identifier. Used by the application code to look up configuration or environment variables. Must be unique system-wide and limited to ASCII alphanumeric with underscores.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Value assigned to the key. Can be interpreted by business logic as a boolean, integer, string, URI, or other serializable data type as needed by configuration context.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional human-readable explanation describing the business purpose, intended usage, and possible values of this setting.

plainFields.name: version
plainFields.description: Monotonic version number incremented with any setting update. Allows implementation of configuration reload, rollback, or audit scenarios.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating when the setting was created. Used for lifecycle tracking and change audits.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update to this configuration record. Reflects operational changes to settings or value modifications.

models.name: todo_list_users
models.description:
Registered user accounts for the Todo List application.

Each user is an independent actor who can manage their own personal todos. The model stores core identity and authentication details, including a unique email address and a securely stored password hash. Profile management features such as display name are provided for personalization, subject to length constraints. Account lifecycle and security are handled via soft deletion and timestamp fields. Only this entity serves as the origin of ownership for user-created data in the system. Soft deletion supports user-driven deactivation or admin suspension. User accounts are never accessible by other users, and all business logic enforces strict isolation of user data across the application.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for authentication. Must conform to RFC standards and be unique across all users.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Secure, one-way hash of the user password. Plain-text passwords are never stored.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: User's visible profile name. Must be 2–50 characters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for the most recent profile change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for when the account was soft deleted (voluntary or admin-initiated).

models.name: todo_list_user_sessions
models.description:
Authentication session records for users.

Each session represents a single login or authentication event for a user. Sessions track login context including IP address, connection URL, and referrer as required for audit and compliance. Unique to each user, allowing multiple concurrent sessions. Expiration field is provided for immediate or scheduled logout. All session objects are managed through this table to maintain strict traceability, session duration control, and regulatory audit logging. Sessions never store tokens or device fingerprints, only raw connection context and timestamps.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the owning user account. {@link todo_list_users.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address at login.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL at login.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL at session start.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expired or was explicitly ended.

models.name: todo_list_admins
models.description:
Administrative accounts for system management and oversight.

Admins maintain overall system health, enforce business rules, audit user activity, and respond to support incidents. Each admin account includes unique identification via email and secure password storage. Admins do not create personal todos, but their actions are logged for traceability and compliance. The model supports soft deletion for account revocation or security purposes. All privileged operations, such as user suspension and audit log access, are performed under an authenticated admin identity.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address for admin authentication. Must conform to RFC standards and be unique among admins.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Secure one-way hash of the admin's password. Never stored in plain text.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Visible admin profile name used for identification in audit logs. Must be 2–50 characters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for account creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for most recent profile or credential update.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for soft deletion (revocation/suspension/voluntary exit).

models.name: todo_list_admin_sessions
models.description:
Authentication session records for administrators.

Each record represents a single login session for an admin account, including IP, connection URL, and referrer details for compliance and security auditing. Sessions enable tracing of every admin action to an authenticated session and identity. Expiration datetime supports scheduled or manual logout. Multiple concurrent sessions are allowed for administrative flexibility. All privileged system operations are executed in the context of a session in this table. No personal data beyond session context and actor reference is stored here.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the owning admin account. {@link todo_list_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address at session start.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL used by the admin at login.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL for audit traceability.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for session creation.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expired or was terminated.

models.name: todo_list_todos
models.description:
Main todo item entity for personal task management.

Represents an individual user-owned task, supporting the full lifecycle from creation, update, completion, to (soft) deletion. Each todo belongs exclusively to one authenticated user and is never visible to others except admins. The entity supports fast retrieval, multi-field filtering, case-insensitive searching, and provides all audit and business timestamps required for compliance and lifecycle tracking.

Field structure enforces domain rules: only non-deleted todos may share the same title for a user, completion is timestamped, and filtered list views are optimized by indexes. Temporal fields (created_at, updated_at, completed_at, deleted_at) allow robust retention, undo, and audit patterns as needed by the product.

Foreign keys, constraints, and indexes ensure data integrity and high query performance for typical CRUD and search operations.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies the todo item.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: User who owns this todo. References {@link todo_list_users.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Short title of the todo item. Required, 1-100 visible UTF-8 characters, trimmed of whitespace. Uniqueness enforced per user among non-deleted todos.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional extended description of the todo item. Up to 1000 characters. May be null or empty.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Todo status in business workflow. Allowed values: 'pending', 'completed'. Only these two values are valid in minimal version; future states can be added with migration.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was marked as completed. Null if not completed.

plainFields.name: created_at

### `todo_list_system_settings`

System-wide application configuration and global settings table.

Provides a centralized location for storing key/value pairs, flags, and
operational parameters used by the todo list application at runtime. Each
row represents a distinct configuration setting. This allows for
reliable, auditable modification and retrieval of system-level options,
feature toggles, and environment variables.

Typical usage includes storing site-wide feature switches, maintenance
flags, version numbers, and other application settings that need to be
referenced by business logic or admin operations. Settings can be updated
as the product evolves or undergoes upgrades, with timestamps preserving
the history of changes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key. Uniquely identifies each configuration record.
- `key`
  > Unique setting identifier. Used by the application code to look up
  > configuration or environment variables. Must be unique system-wide and
  > limited to ASCII alphanumeric with underscores.
- `value`
  > Value assigned to the key. Can be interpreted by business logic as a
  > boolean, integer, string, URI, or other serializable data type as needed
  > by configuration context.
- `description`
  > Optional human-readable explanation describing the business purpose,
  > intended usage, and possible values of this setting.
- `version`
  > Monotonic version number incremented with any setting update. Allows
  > implementation of configuration reload, rollback, or audit scenarios.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp indicating when the setting was created. Used for lifecycle
  > tracking and change audits.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of last update to this configuration record. Reflects
  > operational changes to settings or value modifications.

### `todo_list_users`

Registered user accounts for the Todo List application.

Each user is an independent actor who can manage their own personal
todos. The model stores core identity and authentication details,
including a unique email address and a securely stored password hash.
Profile management features such as display name are provided for
personalization, subject to length constraints. Account lifecycle and
security are handled via soft deletion and timestamp fields. Only this
entity serves as the origin of ownership for user-created data in the
system. Soft deletion supports user-driven deactivation or admin
suspension. User accounts are never accessible by other users, and all
business logic enforces strict isolation of user data across the
application.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Unique email address used for authentication. Must conform to RFC
  > standards and be unique across all users.
- `password_hash`
  > Secure, one-way hash of the user password. Plain-text passwords are never
  > stored.
- `display_name`: User's visible profile name. Must be 2–50 characters.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the user account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for the most recent profile change.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp for when the account was soft deleted (voluntary or
  > admin-initiated).

### `todo_list_user_sessions`

Authentication session records for users.

Each session represents a single login or authentication event for a
user. Sessions track login context including IP address, connection URL,
and referrer as required for audit and compliance. Unique to each user,
allowing multiple concurrent sessions. Expiration field is provided for
immediate or scheduled logout. All session objects are managed through
this table to maintain strict traceability, session duration control, and
regulatory audit logging. Sessions never store tokens or device
fingerprints, only raw connection context and timestamps.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_list_user_id`: Reference to the owning user account. [todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users).
- `ip`: IP address at login.
- `href`: Connection URL at login.
- `referrer`: Referrer URL at session start.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the session was created.
- `expired_at`: Timestamp when the session expired or was explicitly ended.

### `todo_list_admins`

Administrative accounts for system management and oversight.

Admins maintain overall system health, enforce business rules, audit user
activity, and respond to support incidents. Each admin account includes
unique identification via email and secure password storage. Admins do
not create personal todos, but their actions are logged for traceability
and compliance. The model supports soft deletion for account revocation
or security purposes. All privileged operations, such as user suspension
and audit log access, are performed under an authenticated admin
identity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Unique email address for admin authentication. Must conform to RFC
  > standards and be unique among admins.
- `password_hash`: Secure one-way hash of the admin's password. Never stored in plain text.
- `display_name`
  > Visible admin profile name used for identification in audit logs. Must be
  > 2–50 characters.
- `created_at`: Timestamp for account creation.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for most recent profile or credential update.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp for soft deletion (revocation/suspension/voluntary exit).

### `todo_list_admin_sessions`

Authentication session records for administrators.

Each record represents a single login session for an admin account,
including IP, connection URL, and referrer details for compliance and
security auditing. Sessions enable tracing of every admin action to an
authenticated session and identity. Expiration datetime supports
scheduled or manual logout. Multiple concurrent sessions are allowed for
administrative flexibility. All privileged system operations are executed
in the context of a session in this table. No personal data beyond
session context and actor reference is stored here.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_list_admin_id`: Reference to the owning admin account. [todo_list_admins.id](#todo_list_admins).
- `ip`: IP address at session start.
- `href`: Connection URL used by the admin at login.
- `referrer`: Referrer URL for audit traceability.
- `created_at`: Timestamp for session creation.
- `expired_at`: Timestamp when the session expired or was terminated.

### `todo_list_todos`

Main todo item entity for personal task management.

Represents an individual user-owned task, supporting the full lifecycle
from creation, update, completion, to (soft) deletion. Each todo belongs
exclusively to one authenticated user and is never visible to others
except admins. The entity supports fast retrieval, multi-field filtering,
case-insensitive searching, and provides all audit and business
timestamps required for compliance and lifecycle tracking.

Field structure enforces domain rules: only non-deleted todos may share
the same title for a user, completion is timestamped, and filtered list
views are optimized by indexes. Temporal fields (created_at, updated_at,
completed_at, deleted_at) allow robust retention, undo, and audit
patterns as needed by the product.

Foreign keys, constraints, and indexes ensure data integrity and high
query performance for typical CRUD and search operations.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies the todo item.
- `todo_list_user_id`: User who owns this todo. References [todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users).
- `title`
  > Short title of the todo item. Required, 1-100 visible UTF-8 characters,
  > trimmed of whitespace. Uniqueness enforced per user among non-deleted
  > todos.
- `description`
  > Optional extended description of the todo item. Up to 1000 characters.
  > May be null or empty.
- `status`
  > Todo status in business workflow. Allowed values: 'pending', 'completed'.
  > Only these two values are valid in minimal version; future states can be
  > added with migration.
- `completed_at`: Timestamp when the todo was marked as completed. Null if not completed.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp of the todo item. Set when the record is first created.
- `updated_at`
  > Last modification timestamp. Updated on every change of title,
  > description, or status.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp. Null if not deleted; set when user deletes the
  > todo for retention/undo window.

### `todo_list_audit_logs`

System audit log entries for privileged administrative events and
compliance tracking.

Captures every significant admin action or sensitive event affecting user
data or system configuration. Each entry includes the precise actor
(admin or system service), affected target (user or resource), event
type/category, timestamp, and an optional narrative or details for audit
clarity.

Serves as an immutable, append-only history to ensure legal and business
compliance—supporting forensics, investigation, and external audit. No
audit event can be changed or deleted. Foreign keys reference existing
administrator and user tables for actor/target traceability. Optimized
for search and filterability on date, actor, target, and event type.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key. Unique identifier for each audit event.
- `admin_id`
  > Administrator responsible for the event. References {@link
  > todo_list_admins.id}.
- `target_user_id`
  > (Optional) User account affected by the event. May be null if event does
  > not target a specific user. References [todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users).
- `event_type`
  > The type or category of event (e.g., 'user_deletion', 'todo_removed',
  > 'permission_changed', 'login_failed', 'system_restart'). Must be a short,
  > machine-readable string.
- `event_time`
  > Precise timestamp of when the event occurred (in UTC ISO8601; required
  > for every entry).
- `details`
  > Optional narrative or context describing the event (who, what, why, and
  > business reason for privileged interventions). Up to 2000 characters.

operations.specification: This operation registers a new user in the Todo List application using the primary table todo_list_users. It requires a unique email address and a secure password—passwords are stored as one-way hashes. Optionally, a display name is included for user personalization, following all field constraints in the schema. Registration triggers a confirmation email workflow, and subsequent confirmation is required before login is permitted. Security requirements mandate strong validation (email pattern, password length, uniqueness). This endpoint will create a new user record in todo_list_users, set all timestamps, and ensure account is initially active (not soft-deleted). Only non-registered individuals may call this endpoint. No other profile or admin features are accessible at this stage. This endpoint’s logic must be strictly isolated from login or session management operations.
operations.description:
This endpoint enables the registration of a new user by inserting a record into the todo_list_users table. It collects the unique email address (validated for correct structure and uniqueness), a plain-text password (securely hashed and never stored directly), and an initial display_name within 2–50 characters. The endpoint follows the business requirement that registration rejects duplicate emails and sends a confirmation email upon success. Accounts remain in a pending state until confirmed via email. The system records created_at and updated_at timestamps at creation and ensures deleted_at remains null for active users. Soft deletion is not applied at registration.

Role-based access ensures only unauthenticated individuals may register. Security logic prevents access to this endpoint by logged-in users. Upon success, the endpoint returns a JWT access token and refresh token for use in subsequent requests, encoding the user's id, role, and permissions as specified by requirements. This operation is not related to session termination or authentication validation flows.

Field-level validation is enforced: email must match RFC standards and display_name must be 2–50 chars. The operation guarantees no side effects on other system entities or resources. This API operation is required as a system entry point for all standard users and is not used for any admin accounts or privilege escalation workflows.

Error handling addresses duplicate email, invalid data formats, and internal processing issues, returning specific error messages for each scenario. Related operations: login (for authentication), password reset (not implemented here), and refresh (token renewal).

Email and password are validated against stored entries (password compared as hash), and on success, the user receives a new JWT access token and refresh token. Business rules require only users with confirmed email (see registration logic) are permitted to login. Rate limiting ensures accounts are locked for 15 minutes after five consecutive failed attempts, as tracked and enforced by business logic. Security and audit requirements mandate no password or sensitive data is ever exposed in error messages or logs. This operation does not affect admin or privileged session handling; only todo_list_users logins are authorized here. Session tokens encode user id, role, and permissions, as specified in requirements.

This endpoint authenticates a user against their credentials as stored in the todo_list_users table. Email must match an existing active account and password is validated via secure hash comparison. The system enforces a lockout after five failed consecutive attempts, recording lockouts in business state rather than on the schema directly—this should be considered in provider logic. Only accounts with deleted_at null (not soft-deleted) may login. On successful authentication, JWT tokens are returned per security requirements—including role and permission information. The endpoint ensures separation from admin authentication and never exposes internals of failed login attempts to the user, maintaining strict RFC-compliant email and password validation. User permissions are determined by the role at login. This operation does not invoke or affect registration, profile management, or privilege workflows.

Lockout, provisioning of fresh access/refresh tokens, and email confirmation are all critical business logic components and enforced in the provider, not by schema flags. Error handling provides clear feedback: lockout status, invalid credentials, inactive/deleted accounts. Related endpoints: join (user registration), refresh (renewal of tokens), logout (session invalidation, not included here).

This API implements essential security protocol for session longevity—tokens are short-lived and must be periodically refreshed to maintain secure user sessions. The endpoint handles all necessary verification procedures—refresh token integrity, expiry, blacklisting/invalidated status, and ensures user’s status is checked per latest state. No new user credentials are required (email/password not re-entered); the operation strictly validates the refresh token and issues new access/refresh tokens accordingly.

If the user is now soft-deleted or under lockout, token renewal fails and the session should be terminated. Error handling returns clear diagnostic responses for invalid or expired tokens, suspended accounts, or security failures. It is associated with the todo_list_admins Prisma table, which defines administrator credentials, profile fields, and authentication requirements for system-level oversight. Registration data is securely validated according to the schema's constraints—such as required email and password fields—ensuring only properly structured records are inserted. No pre-existing authentication is required, but registration will apply necessary business logic validations and uniqueness checks at the database level.

Administrative roles created via this endpoint are provisioned with appropriate privileges, allowing for subsequent system management actions. The issuance of authorization tokens uses secure, stateless mechanisms, compatible with both further login attempts and refresh workflows.

parameters.name: key

responseBody.description: The deleted configuration record, confirming removal from the database. Returns all fields present prior to deletion.

authorizations.name: user

authorizations.name: admin

token expires, extending the user's session.

IAuthorizationToken.description:

returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

ITodoListUser.IJoin.description:
DTO for user registration in the Todo List system.

Required in the POST /auth/user/join endpoint to create a new user account. Includes all information needed for account creation, session context (audit/security), and business rule enforcement for email, password, and display name.

id.description:
The unique identifier (UUID) of the user account just registered or authenticated.

Primary key of the todo_list_users table. Used across all API operations for scoping ownership and security.

email.description: The user's unique email address for reference in responses where user context is returned upon join, login, or refresh.

display_name.description: The user's display name for profile and presentation. This matches the profile value from registration.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for the most recent profile update or credential change.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp for when the account was soft deleted; null if active or never deleted.

Soft deletion preserves user data for potential recovery or compliance audits instead of irreversible physical removal. A null value means the account is active. Only set by user-initiated deletion or administrative suspension.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
DTO containing authorized session information for the user after join, login, or refresh.

Returned from endpoints such as POST /auth/user/join, /auth/user/login, and /auth/user/refresh, this DTO provides essential identity and session data, including JWT tokens. Sensitive credentials and password hashes are strictly omitted in compliance with the security and privacy requirements.

email.description: Unique email address used for authentication. Must conform to RFC standards. Required to login.

password.description: Plaintext password for authentication. This value is never persisted or logged. Must meet minimum complexity requirements and is validated before login is permitted.

href.description: Connection URL of the login page. This is the URL from which the login attempt was made. Required for session context and security audit trails.

referrer.description: Referrer URL or the previous page visited by the client before the login attempt. Required for session context tracking and security analysis.

ip.description: Client IP address for security and session context. Optional: will be inferred by the backend if not provided by the client; provided in server-side rendering or proxy scenarios.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
Login credentials for authenticating an end user against the todo_list_users entity.

This DTO is used in login operations to receive credentials and necessary session information from clients attempting authentication. Includes email and password for credential validation, and connection context metadata (href, referrer, optional ip) for session creation, security auditing, and compliance. Email must match a registered, active account (deleted_at is null). Password is validated against securely stored hash. Session context fields (href, referrer, ip) are mandatory for self-login operations as per security policy.

Do not include any fields related to account role, ID, session token, or system attributes—authentication context is determined by business logic after credential validation.

refresh_token.description: Current refresh token value for the session renewal request. Submitted by the client; short-lived token issued at login, must be verified for authenticity and validity.

href.description: Connection URL where the refresh was requested. Captured for session tracking and audit purposes.

referrer.description: URL of the page from which the token refresh was initiated. Used for analyzing session flows and security investigations.

ip.description: Client IP address, optionally provided for session context and audit. If omitted, will be inferred by server.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
Request body schema for refreshing a user's session in the Todo List application.

Used to submit a refresh token for session renewal and obtain new JWT tokens. Includes the refresh_token (short-lived, securely managed string) and session context fields (href, referrer, ip) for security auditing.

No credential fields are included—token verification and user status checks are handled by session middleware. Do not include user identity, authentication, or system fields outside of refresh_token and session context.

ITodoListAdmin.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for registering a new admin account for system management.

Fields correspond to the todo_list_admins Prisma table and are strictly validated for security and uniqueness. Used only for onboarding new admin users. Password is received in plain text for hashing during creation. Email and display_name must meet specified constraints and will be checked for uniqueness and valid format. Soft deletion and system fields are excluded from request; all are system-managed. Self-registering actors must provide session context (href/referrer required, ip optional).

email.description: Unique admin email for authentication. Must comply with RFC email format, and is globally unique among admin accounts.

password.description: Plain text password to be securely hashed. Never stored or transmitted except in hashed form; must meet defined security requirements.

display_name.description: Visible admin display/profile name used in logs and the admin UI. Must be 2–50 characters.

href.description: Connection URL (current page) where registration occurs. Required for session/audit trace.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page) for session/audit trace. Required for compliance and traceability.

ip.description: Client IP address at registration. Optional for self-registration; may be extracted server-side if omitted.

ITodoListAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Response DTO for admin authentication: issued after join, login, or refresh.

Includes tokens and basic metadata for authenticated admin access. Used for credential lifecycle operations: join, login, session refresh. No sensitive internal security information is exposed. Conforms to security best practices for authentication responses. The token structure may reference additional JWT or session type components as needed; the id is always the admin uuid.

display_name.description: Admin's display/profile name for identification in logs and UI.

Timestamp (ISO 8601 format) indicating when the admin account was created in the system.

This field is set automatically and never changes, supporting audit trails and compliance requirements.

Reflects the last modification time, which advances on profile or security changes for auditing purposes.

ITodoListAdminSession.ISummary.description:
Summary information for an administrative session/account.

Provides essential fields to identify and display admin actors in audit logs and privileged operation records. Does not include authentication credentials or sensitive fields. Used for list and reference embedding in session or activity-related APIs. Aligns with the todo_list_admins database schema; sensitive fields (like password) are excluded.

Use for lightweight summary of administrative identities and to track responsible parties in privileged operations.

ITodoListAdmin.ILogin.description:
Request DTO for admin authentication.

Represents the input structure for an admin login attempt. Accepts the admin's registered email address and the plain password. Does not include session context fields, as session is established after successful login. Both fields are strictly validated against the admin table constraints, including unique email and password rule enforcement. Used exclusively for admin authentication endpoints, not for profile editing or registration.

email.description: Admin's registered email address for authentication. Must correspond exactly to a unique value in the todo_list_admins table. Validated against RFC standards. Required for login.

password.description: Admin's plain password submitted for credential verification. Never stored or logged in plaintext. Backend will hash and compare value using the stored password_hash in database.

ITodoListAdmin.IRefresh.description:
Request DTO for admin session refresh.

Accepts the admin JWT refresh token for validating and renewing administrator authentication state. Used to extend or resume admin sessions in accordance with session and security policies. Field constraints are governed by the session model, and the provided refresh token is strictly validated before new authentication tokens are issued. No personal or credential data submitted; only the refresh token tied to the relevant admin session context is included. Used solely for admin session continuity, separate from login and registration operations.

refresh_token.description: The JWT refresh token linked to the current admin session. Used to request a new access/refresh token pair by verifying session validity and compliance with business rules.

id.description:
Primary key for the user account.

Represents the unique, system-generated identifier for each user in the Todo List application. All APIs and internal references use this value as the authoritative user reference. Must always be a valid UUID (RFC 4122 format), auto-generated at account creation.

Used to establish ownership for all user-created todos and session records. Never changes after initial creation.

email.description:
Email address used for authentication, must be unique and RFC compliant.

Every user account must have a unique email conforming to standard Internet email formats. This ensures reliable communication, account recovery, and unique login identity for each user.

The system enforces uniqueness and rejects attempts to register duplicate email addresses.

display_name.description:
User's visible profile name for display and personalization.

Used in all personal todo views, account screens, and optional sharing features. Length is enforced strictly between 2 and 50 characters to ensure usability and avoid display issues.

created_at.description:
Timestamp representing when the user account was first created (UTC ISO8601).

Immutable audit field, set automatically by the system at registration. Used for audit and compliance reporting, as well as for account age-based logic.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent change to the user's profile or credentials.

Automatically updated by the system whenever account data is modified. Used for history tracking, cache invalidation, and user notifications.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp for when the account was soft deleted; null if active or never deleted.

Soft deletion preserves user data for potential recovery or compliance audits instead of irreversible physical removal. A null value means the account is active. Only set by user-initiated deletion or administrative suspension.

ITodoListUser.description:
Represents a registered user account for the Todo List application.

Contains core identity and profile information such as unique email (for authentication), display name, account creation and update timestamps. Enforces strict data isolation—each user sees only their own profile and owned data. Used as the owner context for all personal todos and sessions.

Sensitive data such as the password hash is always excluded from API responses. All business logic, validation, and security controls are enforced according to requirements specified for the todo_list_users table.

email.description:
New email to set for this user account, must be unique and RFC compliant.

If specified, the API will validate that the email is unique and valid prior to applying the change. Used for login and notification; changing this triggers notification and may require re-verification.

Cannot be updated to match another user's email. Optional; only present if user is attempting to change their email address.

display_name.description:
New display name for this user, must be 2-50 characters.

Personalization field for the profile. If provided, replaces the user's current display name. API will strictly enforce minimum and maximum length constraints.

Optional; only present when user intends to change their visible name.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
DTO schema for updating editable profile fields of a registered user account in the Todo List application.

Allows self-service or admin-initiated changes to email or display name, with full internal validation according to the requirements of the todo_list_users table. System fields (id, timestamps, password hash, deletion status) are always excluded and cannot be updated through this DTO.

At least one property must be provided for the update operation to have effect; all properties are optional for PATCH/PUT compatibility.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
Authentication session records for users.

Represents a single login or authentication event for a specific user. Tracks login context including IP address, connection URL, and referrer, as required for audit and compliance operations. Each session record is linked to its owning user's account and contains timestamps for creation and (if applicable) expiration.

Does not store tokens or device fingerprints, only connection metadata and time boundaries for strict regulatory audit requirements. Used in security review, login monitoring, and administrative audits. Managed as a subsidiary of the user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the session record. Automatically generated by the database. Used for referencing and deleting specific sessions.

href.description: Connection URL at login. Captures the full page or endpoint through which login was initiated, supporting both audit/compliance and forensic analysis use cases.

referrer.description: Referrer URL at session start. Captures where the user was immediately prior to login, used for traceability and account security investigation.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this session was created. Represents exact login time for compliance, security audits, and timeline reconstruction.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the session expired or was explicitly ended. Nullable; may be null if session is still active.
Null if the session is currently active and has not expired or been explicitly ended.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the session expired or ended, or null if still active.

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description:

Supports pagination (page, limit), filtering by date or status, and text search. Used for both user-facing and administrator access patterns. Designed to ensure search results remain within the authenticated user's permissions or under explicit admin supervision.

Applies strict filtering and sort parameters to support security, compliance, and usability requirements.

Filter by session status: 'active' for currently valid sessions (not expired), 'expired' for sessions that ended or timed out.

Assigned at account creation and immutable for the lifetime of the admin account. Used for audit logging, account management, and in path parameters for all admin-specific API requests.

email.description:
Unique email address used for administrator authentication and communication.

Must conform to email RFC standards and be unique among all admin accounts in the todo_list_admins table. Used as the login credential and for security/audit notifications.

display_name.description:

Must be between 2 and 50 characters. Used for identification in system logs, activity feeds, and dashboards.

Timestamp (ISO 8601) indicating when the admin account was revoked, suspended, or voluntarily deleted.

Populated only for soft-deleted accounts; otherwise null. Used for security reviews and audit tracking.

ITodoListAdmin.description:
Administrator account entity for Todo List system-wide management and oversight.

Represents privileged user identity for auditing, system configuration, and enforcing business rules. Admin accounts are uniquely identified by UUID and managed via secure email/password authentication. Certain fields (such as password hash) are never included in responses for security reasons.

This schema provides all necessary information for privileged platform APIs, compliance audits, and admin dashboards while preserving privacy boundaries for authentication credentials.

email.description: New unique email address for the administrative account, if updating. Must be RFC-compliant and not currently used by another admin. Used in authentication and as a contact point for system notifications.

display_name.description:
New profile display name for the administrator.

Must be between 2 and 50 characters if provided. Used for identification in system audit logs and dashboards.

Clear prior deletion (restore account) or explicitly show as not deleted.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp to mark the admin account as soft-deleted (revoked/suspended) if set. Value should be ISO 8601, or null.

ITodoListAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Request body to update administrator accounts in the Todo List platform.

Fields are all optional and only those provided will be updated. Ownership, account creation and password hash/credentials cannot be changed through this DTO. Used only by privileged admin actors in authenticated system management APIs.

Audit tracking and security policies are enforced on every update; attempts to modify restricted or non-editable fields will result in errors. Password modification must use a dedicated endpoint, not this DTO.

ITodoListAdminSession.description:
Authentication session records for administrators.

Each record represents a single login session for an admin account, including IP, connection URL, and referrer details for compliance and security auditing. Sessions enable tracing of every admin action to an authenticated session and identity. Expiration datetime supports scheduled or manual logout. Multiple concurrent sessions are allowed for administrative flexibility. All privileged system operations are executed in the context of a session in this table. No personal data beyond session context and actor reference is stored here.

ITodoListAdminSession.IRequest.description:

ITodoListAdmin.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an administrative account for system management and oversight.

Represents only core attributes of administrative actors engaged in privileged actions, such as audit log entries, system configuration, or user oversight. Todo status in business workflow. Allowed values: 'pending', 'completed'. Only these two values are valid in minimal version; future states can be added with migration.

ITodoListTodo.description:
Main todo item entity for personal task management.

Represents an individual user-owned task, supporting the full lifecycle from creation, update, completion, to (soft) deletion. Each todo belongs exclusively to one authenticated user and is never visible to others except admins. The entity supports fast retrieval, multi-field filtering, case-insensitive searching, and provides all audit and business timestamps required for compliance and lifecycle tracking.

Field structure enforces domain rules: only non-deleted todos may share the same title for a user, completion is timestamped, and filtered list views are optimized by indexes. Temporal fields (created_at, updated_at, completed_at, deleted_at) allow robust retention, undo, and audit patterns as needed by the product.

Foreign keys, constraints, and indexes ensure data integrity and high query performance for typical CRUD and search operations.

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description:
Criteria object for advanced filtering, searching, and pagination of a user's todo items in task list retrieval operations.

This DTO is not directly mapped to any database table or persistent domain entity; it serves as the API request body for complex query and list search actions. Each property is optional and allows clients to compose sophisticated operations including full-text search, field-based filtering, sorting, and pagination controls.

The structure is extensible for future requirements, and edge cases of field combinations—such as supplying both full-text query and status filter, or omitting all filters for an unconstrained fetch—are fully supported. Maintain API contract discipline when extending this type: new properties must maintain backward compatibility for clients and ensure the same semantics for omitted and null values.

All filtering and pagination logic is handled by the backend, which interprets property presence, absence, or null values according to the business logic described in requirements analysis.

Not mapped directly to any persistent entity.

query.description: Full-text search expression for the todo title or description. If omitted, results are not filtered by content.

oneOf.description: Only include todos with a status of 'pending' in the results.
Only include todos with a status of 'completed' in the results.

created_to.description: Include todos created before or equal to this ISO 8601 datetime (as per RFC 3339). Optional; omit for no upper bound.

completed_from.description: Include todos completed at or after this ISO 8601 datetime (as per RFC 3339). Optional; omit for no lower bound.

completed_to.description: Include todos completed before or equal to this ISO 8601 datetime (as per RFC 3339). Optional; omit for no upper bound.

oneOf.description: Sort results by creation timestamp (default).
Sort results by update timestamp.

Sort in descending order (default).

sort_order.description: Sort order: ascending (asc) or descending (desc). If omitted, defaults to 'desc'.

page.description: 1-based page number for paginated results. Optional; defaults to 1.

page_size.description: Number of records per results page. Optional; default is 20, maximum is 100.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new todo item.

This structure allows clients to specify a short title as a required task identifier and optionally provide an extended description, subject to length limits and unique-per-user constraints. Titles are strictly enforced as unique among all of a user's non-deleted todos, must be 1–100 visible UTF-8 characters, and are trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace. The optional description supports up to 1000 characters, can be omitted entirely, or explicitly provided as null; the backend must recognize the distinction for validation and storage simplicity.

Ownership attribution is server-enforced: the new todo is always attributed to the currently authenticated principal, and this cannot be overridden by the request body.

System-managed fields (status, created_at, updated_at, completed_at, deleted_at, as well as the foreign key to the owning user) are exclusively set by the backend and must not appear in the request. Attempts to supply these fields should be rejected or safely ignored according to the API's error handling policy.

Validation occurs at both API and persistence layers, with business rules for field uniqueness, required/optional distinction, and maximum length enforced end-to-end.

title.description: Short title of the todo item. Required and must be unique for the authenticated user's active (non-deleted) todos. 1–100 UTF-8 characters, stripped of whitespace; cannot be empty or whitespace-only after trimming.

oneOf.description: Optional extended description of the todo item. May be provided as a string (up to 1000 characters), omitted entirely, or set to null. If omitted or null, no description will be stored.
Indicates that no description is being set for this todo. The backend recognizes the absence of a description.

description.description: Optional extended description of the todo item. Maximum 1000 characters. The property may be omitted, explicitly set to null, or contain a textual value. System logic should handle each case accordingly.

status.description: New status of the todo. Allowed values: 'pending' or 'completed'. Status change will set or clear completed_at as appropriate.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for a todo item.

Allows updating the title, description, or status of a todo. Title must remain unique among active todos for the user and 1–100 UTF-8 characters if given. Description can be set (up to 1000 characters), removed (null), or left unchanged. Status must be either 'pending' or 'completed'; business logic ensures proper update of related fields. System-controlled timestamps, completion, and ownership are always handled by the backend; only mutable fields are present here. All fields are optional; if omitted, value remains unchanged.

ITodoListAuditLog.description:
System audit log entry for privileged administrative events and compliance tracking.

Represents a single, immutable log capturing a sensitive administrative action or compliance event within the Todo List application. Each entry includes the administrative actor, potentially affected target user, event category, timestamp, and optional narrative. Used for forensics, legal compliance, and to support investigation workflows. Audit entries cannot be changed or deleted.

Foreign keys reference admin and user tables for traceability. Optimized for search and filter on actor, timestamp, event type, and details. Populated only by the system, never by clients.

id.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for each audit event.

admin.description: Administrator responsible for the event. Actor reference for traceability to system admin.

target_user.description: (Optional) User account affected by the event. If present, references the user entity; otherwise null.

event_type.description: Type/category of the event (e.g., 'user_deletion', 'todo_removed', etc.). Short, machine-readable string.

event_time.description: Precise UTC ISO8601 timestamp for when the event occurred.

details.description: Optional narrative/context for the event (max 2000 chars). Provides business reason, who, what, and why for this privileged event.

ITodoListAuditLog.IRequest.description:
Filter criteria and pagination/sorting parameters for searching audit logs.

Allows filtering by event_time (range), event_type (exact matches), administrator (by ID), affected user (by ID), and keyword search in details narrative. Pagination controls and sorting options enable efficient review of large audit log volumes. Only accessible to admin users.

event_time_range.description: Restricts log results to those within this UTC date-time range. Null for no restriction.

event_types.description: If present, only include specific event types/categories. Array of machine-readable event_type strings.

admin_id.description: If specified, restricts to logs authored by a single admin. UUID referencing admin table. Null for no restriction.

target_user_id.description: If specified, restricts to logs affecting the specified user. UUID referencing user table. Null for no restriction.

search.description: Full-text search keyword for the details field.

page.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 if omitted.

limit.description: Page size (number of entries per page). Defaults to 20, max 200.

sort_descending.description: If true, results are ordered by most-recent event_time first (descending). Defaults to true.

Contains only identifying information necessary for review and investigations, not authentication or full profile fields.

display_name.description: User's display name for UI and logs.

Used to restrict results to audits that occurred between two specific instants, inclusive.

from.description: Start of the range (inclusive), in UTC ISO8601.

to.description: End of the range (inclusive), in UTC ISO8601.

key.description: Unique setting identifier. Used by the application code to look up configuration or environment variables. Must be unique system-wide and limited to ASCII alphanumeric with underscores.
